economy.summary: Voted against House Bill 1500 (2023), which would have raised Pennsylvania's minimum wage.
economy.short: Voted against 2023 bill to raise the minimum wage.

taxes.summary: His campaign says he believes taxes should be low, describes himself as a watchdog for government waste, and advocates greater transparency and government reform.
taxes.short: Says taxes should be low; calls himself waste watchdog.

abortion.summary: Voted for Senate Bill 106 (2022), a proposed constitutional amendment stating there is no constitutional right to taxpayer-funded abortion or other right relating to abortion.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating no constitutional right to abortion.

education.summary: His campaign says he supports ensuring an educational system that gives children a clear path to good-paying careers.
education.short: Supports education giving children a path to good-paying careers.

healthcare.summary: His campaign says he is passionate about cancer research and other healthcare initiatives, and he founded and chairs the General Assembly's bipartisan Cancer Caucus.
healthcare.short: Founded bipartisan Cancer Caucus; emphasizes cancer research initiatives.

energy.summary: In a May 2022 statement supporting a House package of fossil fuel bills, he said Pennsylvania should increase natural gas production and transmission capabilities as part of American-led energy independence.
energy.short: Supports increasing Pennsylvania natural gas production and transmission.

guns.summary: Voted against House Bill 714 (2023), which would expand background checks to additional firearm sales; he also voted against House Bill 1018 (2023), an extreme risk protection order measure.
guns.short: Voted against firearm background-check and extreme-risk-protection bills.

economy.summary: His campaign says his top focus is making life in Pennsylvania more affordable, saying families are squeezed by taxes, housing costs, groceries, and utilities.
economy.short: Says his top focus is making life more affordable.

taxes.summary: His campaign says he would lower the tax burden on working people and cut programs he says do not deliver results, citing $250 million spent on horse racing subsidies.
taxes.short: Would lower working people's taxes; cut horse racing subsidies.

education.summary: At his campaign launch he proposed redirecting money from subsidies he would eliminate toward schools, rural infrastructure, and property tax relief.
education.short: Proposes redirecting eliminated subsidy money toward schools.

healthcare.summary: As part of his affordability agenda he said he would work to lower the cost of essentials including prescription medication; his platform does not otherwise detail a healthcare policy.
healthcare.short: Says he would lower prescription medication and other essential costs.

energy.summary: At his campaign launch he said he would push back on cost increases he attributes to unchecked data center growth.
energy.short: Would push back on costs from unchecked data center growth.
